title: Gentle Walking & Coordination (Example)
description: Illustrative walking-in-place and stepping routine for trying out the player. Not a transcription of the source video.
notes: EXAMPLE ONLY. Movements are a draft based on the general theme (walking and coordination) of the linked video. Exercise order, names, cues and every duration are unverified guesses. Check against the source video and edit before relying on it.

exercises.name: March in Place
exercises.instructions: Stand tall and march in place at an easy pace, arms swinging naturally.

phases.label: March
phases.speech: Start marching in place at a comfortable pace. Let your arms swing.

exercises.name: Heel and Toe Taps
exercises.instructions: Alternate tapping a heel forward and a toe back, switching sides.

phases.label: Heel taps forward
phases.speech: Tap one heel forward, then the other. Keep a steady rhythm.

phases.label: Toe taps back
phases.speech: Now tap your toes behind you, alternating sides.

phases.label: Rest
phases.speech: Rest. Walk gently in place and breathe.

exercises.name: Step Pattern
exercises.instructions: Practice a coordinated stepping pattern: step out, step out, step in, step in.

phases.label: Out, out, in, in
phases.speech: Step right foot out, left foot out, right foot in, left foot in. Repeat.

phases.label: Switch lead foot
phases.speech: Switch to lead with your left foot.

phases.label: Left lead
phases.speech: Left foot out, right foot out, left foot in, right foot in. Repeat.

phases.label: Rest
phases.speech: Rest and get ready for the next movement.

exercises.name: Side Step Touch
exercises.instructions: Step to one side and bring the other foot to meet it, then go the other way.

phases.label: Side step touch
phases.speech: Step to the side and touch, then step back the other way. Add your arms if it feels good.

exercises.name: Cool Down Walk
exercises.instructions: Slow your march down and let your breathing settle.

phases.label: Slow march
phases.speech: Slow your march right down. Breathe in through your nose and out through your mouth.

title: Quick Player Check (Example)
description: A 40-second routine with short phases for checking voice, transitions and controls.
notes: EXAMPLE ONLY. Not exercise guidance; it exists to test the timer and spoken cues quickly.

phases.label: Forward
phases.speech: Make small circles forward with both arms.
